question: Post-mortem lividity that remains fixed and does not blanch when pressure is applied indicates that the body has been in that position for at least 6–8 hours since death, and moving the body after this point will not produce new lividity in dependent areas.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. Fixed, non-blanchable lividity indicates 6–8+ hours have passed since death. Once fixed, the lividity pattern is permanent and does not redistribute with body movement. This is forensically significant: a mismatch between fixed lividity distribution and the position in which a body is found suggests the body was moved after death.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Fixed lividity (non-blanchable, non-shifting) indicates that red blood cells have lysed and haemoglobin has diffused into tissue spaces, typically occurring 6–8 hours after death. After fixation, the distribution pattern reflects the position of the body at the time of fixation, not necessarily at death — and the body cannot develop new lividity in newly dependent areas.
